2.0      Overview
This data book describes the next generation Pentium® solu-          desktop applications. Using FireStar in a full-featured, PCl-
tion from the Mobile division of OPTi. The "FireStar" solution       based notebook allows for designs with zero TTL.
supports 64-bit 6x86-class CPUs and is very highly inte-
                                                                     Figure 2-1 shows the logic modules within the functional
grated, packaged in a single 432-pin BGA (Ball Grid Array).
                                                                     blocks of FireStar.
FireStar is intended as a low-cost yet high-performance note-
book solution that can also be appropriate for use in certain

3.0      Signal Definitions

3.1      Terminology/Nomenclature Conventions
The "#" symbol at the end of a signal name indicates that the      Table 3-1   Signal Definitions Legend
active, or asserted state occurs when the signal is at a low
voltage level. When "#" is not present after the signal name,       Mnemonic      Description
the signal is asserted when at the high voltage level.              CMOS          CMOS-level compatible
The terms "assertion" and "negation" are used extensively.          Dcdr          Decoder
This is done to avoid confusion when working with a mixture
of "active low" and "active high" signals. The term "assert", or    Ext           External
"assertion" indicates that a signal is active, independent of       G             Ground
whether that level is represented by a high or low voltage.
The term "negate", or "negation" indicates that a signal is         I             Input
inactive.                                                           Int           Internal
Some FireStar pins have more than one function. These pins          1/0           Input/Output
can be time-multiplexed, have strap options, or can be
selected via register programming. Included in the signal           Mux           Multiplexer
descriptions is a column titled "Selected By" which explains        0             Output
how to implement/invoke the various functions that a pin may
                                                                    OD            Open drain
have. The terms PCI DVD, PCI DV1, and SYSCFG relate to
registers located in the PCI and System Configuration Regis-        p             Power
ter Spaces of FireStar. Refer to Section 5.0, "Register
                                                                    PD            Pull-down resistor
Descriptions" for more details regarding these register
spaces and their access mechanisms.                                 PU            Pull-up resistor
The tables in this section use several common abbreviations.        s             Schmitt-trigger
Table 3-1 lists the mnemonics and their meanings. Note that         S/T/S         Sustain Tristate
TTL/CMOS/Schmitt-trigger levels pertain to inputs only. Out-
puts are driven at CMOS levels.                                     TTL           TTL-level compatible

3.2.1    CPU Interface Signals Set
                                       Signal Type   Selected
 Signal Name             Pin No.         (Drive)        By      Signal Description

 Host Data Bus

 HD[63:0]             Refer to Table       1/0                  Host Data Bus Lines 63 through 0: Provides a 64-
                      3-2                (4mA)                  bit data path to the CPU.

 CPU Address

 HA[31 :3]            Refer to Table       1/0                  Host Address Bus Lines 31 through 3: HA[31 :3]
                      3-2                (4mA)                  are the address lines of the CPU bus. HA[31 :3] are
                                                                connected to CPU lines A[31 :3]. Along with the byte
                                                                enable signals, HA[31 :3] define the physical area of
                                                                memory or 1/0 being accessed.
                                                                During CPU cycles, the HA[31 :3] lines are inputs.
                                                                They are used for address decoding and second
                                                                level cache tag lookup sequences.
                                                                During inquire cycles, the HA[31 :5] lines are outputs
                                                                to the CPU to snoop the first level cache tags. They
                                                                also are outputs to the L2 cache.
 BE[7:0]#                V4:V1,             I                   Byte Enables 7 through 0: Selects the active byte
                         W4:W1                                  lanes on HD[63:0].
 NMI                       AD5             0                    Non-Maskable Interrupt: This signal is activated
                      Strap option       (4mA)                  when a parity error from a local memory read is
                      pin, refer to                             detected or when the IOCHK# signal from the ISA
                      Table 3-7                                 bus is asserted and the corresponding control bit in
                                                                Port B is also enabled.
 INTR                      AF5             0                    Interrupt Request: INTR is driven to signal the CPU
                      Strap option       (4mA)                  that an interrupt request is pending and needs to be
                      pin, refer to                             serviced. The interrupt controller must be pro-
                      Table 3-7                                 grammed following a reset to ensure that INTR is at
                                                                a known state.
 FERR#                      T1              I                   Floating Point Coprocessor Error: This input
                                                                causes two operations to occur. I RQ13 is triggered
                                                                and IGERR# is enabled. An 1/0 write to Port FOh will
                                                                set IGERR# low when FERR# is low.
 IGERR#                    AC6             1/0                  Ignore Coprocessor Error: Normally high, IGERR#
                      Strap option       (4mA)                  will go low after FERR# goes low and an 1/0 write to
                      pin, refer to                             Port OFOh occurs. When FERR# goes high, IGERR#
                      Table 3-7                                 is driven high.

 CPU Control/Status

 CPU I NIT                 AD6             0                    CPU Initialize: A shutdown cycle or a low-to-high
                                                                transition of 1/0 Port 092h bit 0 will trigger CPUINIT.
                                                                If keyboard emulation is enabled (default), a
                                                                CPUI NIT will be generated when a Port 064h write
                                                                cycle with data FEh is decoded. If keyboard emula-
                                                                tion has been disabled, then this signal will be trig-
                                                                gered when it sees the KBRST from the keyboard.

 M/10#            Y5           I                      Memory/Input-Output: M/10#, DIC#, and W/R#
                                                      define CPU bus cycles. Interrupt acknowledge
                                                      cycles are forwarded to the PCI bus as PCI interrupt
                                                      acknowledge cycles. All 1/0 cycles and any memory

                                                      the DRAM interface are forwarded to PCI.

 INV                          0                       Invalidate: Pin AA5 also serves as an output signal
                            (4mA)                     and is used as INV for L 1 cache during an inquire
                                                      cycle.
ADS#              V5           I                      Address Strobe: The CPU asserts ADS# to indi-
                                                      cate that a new bus cycle is beginning. ADS# is
                                                      driven active in the same clock as the address, byte
                                                      enables, and cycle definition signals.
                                                      ADS# has an internal pull-up resistor that is disabled
                                                      when the system is in the Suspend mode.
 BROY#            U5          0                       Burst Ready: BROY# indicates that the system has
                            (4mA)                     responded in one of three ways:
                                                      1) Valid data has been placed on the CPU data bus
                                                         in response to a read,
                                                      2) CPU write data has been accepted by the sys-
                                                         tern, or
                                                      3) the system has responded to a special cycle.
 NA#              U4          0                       Next Address: This signal is connected to the
                            (4mA)                     CPU's NA# pin to request pipelined addressing for
                                                      local memory cycle. FireStar asserts NA# for one
                                                      clock when the system is ready to accept a new
                                                      address from the CPU, even if all data transfers for
                                                      the current cycle have not completed.
 KEN#             R2          0                       Cache Enable: This pin is connected to the KEN#
                            (4mA)                     input of the CPU and is used to determine whether
                                                      the current cycle is cacheable.
 EADS#            T4          0         Cycle         External Address Strobe: This output indicates
                            (4mA)       Multiplexed   that a valid address has been driven onto the CPU
                                                      address bus by an external device. This address will
                                                      be used to perform an internal cache inquiry cycle
                                                      when the CPU samples EADS# active.
WB/WT#                                                Writeback/Write-Through: Pin T4 is also used to
                                                      control writeback or write-through policy for the pri-
                                                      mary cache during CPU cycles.
 HITM#            R4           I                      Hit Modified: Indicates that the CPU has had a hit
                                                      on a modified line in its internal cache during an
                                                      inquire cycle. It is used to prepare for writeback.

 C/BE[3:0]#     AE14,         1/0                  PCI Bus Command and Byte Enables: During the
                AF14,        (PCI)                 address phase of a transaction, C/BE[3:0]# define
                AC15,                              the PCI command. During the data phase,
                AD15                               C/BE[3:0]# are used as the PCI byte enables. The
                                                   PCI commands indicate the current cycle type, and
                                                   the PCI byte enables indicate which byte lanes carry
                                                   meaningful data. FireStar drives C/BE[3:0]# as an
                                                   initiator of a PCI bus cycle and monitors C/BE[3:0]#
                                                   as a target.
 CPAR           AC17          1/0                  Calculated Parity Signal: PAR is "even" parity and
                             (PCI)                 is calculated on 36 bits - AD[31 :O] plus C/BE[3:0]#.
                                                   PAR is generated for address and data phases and
                                                   is only guaranteed to be valid on the PCI clock after
                                                   the corresponding address or data phase.
 FRAME#          AB9          1/0                  Cycle Frame: FRAME# is driven by the current bus
                             (PCI)                 master to indicate the beginning and duration of an
                                                   access. FRAME# is asserted to indicate that a bus
                                                   transaction is beginning. FRAME# is an input when
                                                   FireStar is the target and an output when it is the ini-
                                                   tiator.
 IRDY#           AB11         1/0                  Initiator Ready: IRDY# indicates FireStar's ability,
                             (PCI)                 as an initiator, to complete the current data phase of
                                                   the transaction. It is used in conjunction with
                                                   TROY#. A data phase is completed on each clock
                                                   that both IRDY# and TROY# are sampled asserted.
                                                   I ROY# is an input to when Fire Star is the target and
                                                   an output when it is the initiator.
 TROY#          AB12          1/0                  Target Ready: TROY# indicates FireStar's ability to
                             (PCI)                 complete the current data phase of the transaction.
                                                   It is used in conjunction with I ROY#. A data phase is
                                                   completed on each clock that TROY# and IRDY#
                                                   are both sampled asserted. TROY# is an input when
                                                   FireStar is the initiator and an output when it is the
                                                   target.
 DEVSEL#         AF15         1/0                  Device Select: FireStar asserts DEVSEL# to claim
                             (PCI)                 a PCI transaction. As an output, FireStar asserts
                                                   DEVSEL# when it samples configuration cycles to
                                                   the configuration registers. FireStar also asserts
                                                   DEVSEL# when an internal IPC address is decoded.
                                                   As an input, DEVSEL# indicates the response to a
                                                   transaction. If no slave claims the cycle, FireStar will
                                                   assert DEVSEL# to terminate the cycle.
 STOP#          AC16          1/0                  Stop: STOP# indicates that FireStar, as a target, is
                             (PCI)                 requesting a master to stop the current transaction.
                                                   As a master, STOP# causes FireStar to stop the
                                                   current transaction. STOP# is an output when
                                                   FireStar is a target and an input when it is the initia-
                                                   tor.

4.6.4       DRAM Buffering                                              4.6.4.1     CPU-to-DRAM Deep Buffer
Deep buffering is one of the major performance enhance-                 A six quad-word deep FIFO is built into the DBC in the CPU-
ments in FireStar. It incorporates deep buffers in the CPU-to-          to-DRAM path. These deep buffers are used by FireStar to
DRAM and PCl-to-DRAM data paths, which enables read                     buffer CPU-to-DRAM data. Once the DRAM is free, the buff-
prefetching and write posting in the data paths.                        ered data is dispatched into the DRAM. This way the system
                                                                        level latencies caused by shared resources are minimized.
• Deep buffering for DRAM performance
  - Six quad-word CPU-to-DRAM write posting                             4.6.4.2     PCl-to-DRAM Deep Buffer
  - 24 double-word PCl-to-DRAM write posting                            A 24 double-word buffer has been designed into the PCl-to-
  - 24 double-word DRAM-to-PCI read prefetch                            DRAM path. During PCI master write bursts, the master posts
                                                                        data into this buffer. Once CPU-to-DRAM cycles are com-
Table 4-28 lists the registers/bits that are associated with            pleted, the posted data will be written back in to the DRAM.
DRAM Buffering.                                                         This avoids any stalling in the PCI and full bus bandwidth is
                                                                        utilized.

4.6.6.3    DRAM Refresh Logic                                   The DRAM controller arbitrates between CPU DRAM
FireStar supports the following types of refresh schemes:       accesses and DRAM refresh cycles, while the ISA bus con-
• Normal refresh                                                troller arbitrates between CPU accesses to the ISA bus, OMA
• Non-ISA refresh                                               and ISA refresh. The ISA bus controller asserts the RFSH#
• Burst refresh                                                 and MRD# commands and outputs the refresh address dur-
                                                                ing ISA bus refresh cycles.
During normal refresh, the CPU bus is put on BOFF# and the
DRAM bus is refreshed. This is the default condition at         FireStar implements refresh cycles to the local DRAM using

Claiming ISA Cycles
Because ISA does not provide any acknowledgment that a
cycle was claimed by a local device, the 82C825 logic uses a
special protocol to determine whether or not to claim the
cycle.
Positive ISA Decode: The 82C825 logic waits to determine
whether the peripheral device has responded by asserting
M16#, 1016#, or NOWS#, or by deasserting IOCHRDY. Any
of these signalling events indicates that an ISA device is
responding to the cycle and the 82C825 logic can positively
claim the cycle without waiting for its completion. These
events can be individually masked through 82C825 program-
ming if desired.

       will return to Continuous mode. PCIDV1 BBh[7] can be read to determine the current state of the logic.

events to be flagged even if they are not programmed to gen-           these events to be registered. Reading this register returns
erate an SMI. In this way, code can check whether a key-               flags indicating whether any of the events have taken place
stroke occurred since the last time the register was checked,          and automatically resets the entire register. The register can
for example, without actually generating an SMI for every              be written if desired to set the selected bits. In this way, a
keystroke.                                                             read-modify-write code sequence can be used to clear

4.17     System Management Interrupt (SMI)
The 3.3V Pentium processor offers a System Management                   FireStar handles 39 Power Management Interrupt (PMI)
Interrupt (SMI) that allows external logic to signal to the CPU         events that can be selectively enabled to cause an SMI to the
that a high priority event has occurred and must be serviced            CPU. Since some of these PMI events are actually a single
but should not in any way interfere with the application cur-           indication from a group of events (such as a single PMI #6
rently being processed. When the CPU senses its SMI# input              that indicates whether any of the selected I RQ lines has gone
active, it saves the context of its current application and loads       active), the effective number of events that can be indicated
the context of its System Management Mode (SMM) handler                 is actually much greater than 39.
routine from a protected part of RAM. SMM code can then
                                                                        The PMI events that can be programmed to generate an SMI
proceed to determine the reason for the interrupt, service it
                                                                        are listed in Table 4-152.
appropriately, and return to application processing through a
special RESUME instruction that restores the context as it
originally was before the SMI.

  #36      Serial IRQ        An SMI has been signalled by a device using the serial interrupt line.
  #37      DMA_ACCESS        A OMA controller register is being accessed
  #38      IRQ_DRIVEBACK An SMI has been signalled by a device using IRQ driveback.

SYSCFG 13h[3] and 14h[3] are used as follows when the CPU is not in SMM:

• 13h[3] = O:
  - No relocation. This setting prevents application software from accessing SMI memory space.

• 13h[3] = 1:
  - If 14h[3] = 1, CPU addresses in the AOOOh-BOOOh segments go to SMI memory space - the DRAM segments at AOOOh-
    BOOOh. This setting provides the mechanism for initially loading SMI code to the AOOOh-BOOOh region.
  - If 14h[3] = 0, the AOOOh-BOOOh area in DRAM cannot be accessed.
The significance of 14h[3] during SMM is explained in Section 4.17.1.2, "Run-Time SMI Address Relocation".

The BIOS sets 13h[3] = 1 and 14h[3] = 1. It can then load code and data into DRAM segments AOOOh and BOOOh. This first load
operation must be addressed to the AOOOh and BOOOh segments. Upon completing the loading of all initial SMM code and data,
the BIOS clears 14h[3] to 0 to protect the SMM space.

(1) In a situation where there is a PCl-to-PCI bridge in a system and that bridge supports write posting, the following deadlock condition can
    occur. The bridge posts data from a master on the secondary PCI bus into its FIFO. If at the same time the 82C700 is accessing the bridge
    as a target, then the bridge will tell the 82C700 to retry its request after it has serviced out its FIFO. This will result in a deadlock situation.
    Bit 3 needs to be set to 1 if an OP1i 82C824 or 82C814 bridge, or a DEC 21050 PCl-to-PCI bridge (or a similar chip) is used.

PCIDVO 08h                                                Revision Identification Register (RO)                                      Default= 10h
   - The chip revision number in the PCI configuration space consists of two parts: a major revision number and a minor revision number. The
     8-bit register is interpreted as x.yh, where for example revision 2.1 of the chip would be read as two BCD digits, 0010 0001 b. Software
     programmers must take care in using the minor revision number, because the number may change between register- and software-
     equivalent versions of the chip.

5.3        PCIDV1 Register Space
The PCI Configuration Register Space designated as                       PCI DV1 00h-3Fh are PCl-specific related registers while
PCIDV1 is accessed through Configuration Mechanism #1 as                 PCI DV1 40h-FFh are system control related registers. Table
Bus #0, Device #1, and Function #0.                                      5-8 gives the bit formats for these registers.

PCIDV1 08h                                                Revision Identification Register (RO)                                 Default= 10h
   - The chip revision number in the PCI configuration space consists of two parts: a major revision number and a minor revision number. The
     8-bit register is interpreted as x.yh, where for example revision 2.1 of the chip would be read as two BCD digits, 0010 0001 b. Software
     programmers must take care in using the minor revision number, because the number may change between register- and software-
     equivalent versions of the chip.

PCIDV1 54h                              IRQ Driveback Address Register - Byte O: Address Bits [7:0]                                Default= OOh
   IRQ driveback protocol address bits [7:0]:
   - When an external device logic, such as the 82C824 PC Card Controller or the 82C814 Docking Controller, must generate an interrupt
     from any source, it follows the IRQ Driveback Protocol and toggles the REQ# line to the 82C700. Once it has the bus, it writes the
     changed IRQ information to the 32-bit 1/0 address specified in this register. The 82C700 interrupt controller claims this cycle and latches
     the new IRQ values.
   - This register defaults to a value of OOh, which disables the IRQ driveback scheme.
PCIDV1 55h                             IRQ Driveback Address Register - Byte 1: Address Bits [15:8]                                Default= OOh

PCIDV1 56h                             IRQ Driveback Address Register - Byte 2: Address Bits [23:16]                               Default= OOh

PCIDV1 57h                             IRQ Driveback Address Register - Byte 3: Address Bits [31 :24]                              Default= OOh


PCIDV1 58h                            DRQ Remap Base Address Register - Byte O: Address Bits [7:0]                                 Default= OOh
   DRQ remap base address bits [7:0]:
   - The distributed OMA protocol requires OMA controller registers for each OMA channel to be individually mapped into 1/0 space outside
     the range claimed by ISA devices. Bits A[31 :O] of this register specify that base; bits 6:0 are reserved (write 0) because the base address
     can fall only on 128 byte boundaries. The 82C700 logic uses this base address two ways:
      1) to claim accesses to a PCM CIA OMA controller channel;
      2) to forward accesses across the bridge to remote devices specified in the OMA Channel Selector Register.

Note: The bits in the ACPI Source Status Register (Bytes 0 and 1) indicate the current state of the ACPI lines, either the discrete pins or the
      last IRQ Driveback value depending on the ACPI Source Control Register setting. This information may also be available elsewhere,
      since the IRQ Driveback values and PIO pin values can be read from other registers. However, this register provides a central means of
      reading signal state and is especially useful for signals such as LID (which generates an SCI, System Controller Interrupt, on both
      opening and closing events).

Offset 08h-0Ah                                        TMR_VAL -Timer Value Register (RO)
   Bits [23:0] correspond to: [7:0] = 08h, [15:8] = 09h, [23:16] = OAh
   The timer is a free-running "up" counter based on the 14MHz clock divided by 4. It runs whenever the 14MHz input clock to FireStar
   is present, and is cleared to 0 whenever PCIRST# is asserted. Whenever TMR_VAL[23] changes from O-to-1 or from 1-to-O, the
   TMR_STS bit is set to 1; writing 1 back to TMR_STS clears the bit. If TMR_EN = 1 when TMR_STS = 1, an SCI occurs (if globally
   enabled).
   - Bits [23:0] =A read-only value that returns the power management timer count. The count is based on 14.3181 SMHz/4. The count is
     cleared by a PCI bus reset. Whenever bit 23 toggles, TMR_STS is set to indicate the event. Counts only while the system is active.

specification are not implied.

Appendix A. Compact ISA Specification
This document describes a new OPTi interface that will be           • SA[23:0] (24 pins)
used to interface the 82C852 PCMCIA Controller to OPTi
                                                                    • IORD#, IOWR#, MRD#, MWR#, SMRD#, SMWR#,
system controller chipsets. This interface may also be used to
                                                                      SBHE#, NOWS#, AEN, 1016#, M16# (11 pins)
interface OPTi peripheral products in the future. The interface
is OPTi-proprietary, and may be licensed to others in the           • IRQ3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15; DRQ/DACK#O, 1, 2, 3,
future.                                                               5, 6, 7, and TC (25 pins)
                                                                    Compact ISA defines only two new signals, CMD# and SEL#/
A.1      Compact ISA Overview                                       ATB#, for a total requirement of 22 pins. The pin count reduc-
The Compact ISA interface coexists with the standard ISA            tion over standard ISA is 58 pins. Compact ISA performance
interface. Chips that support the Compact ISA interface enjoy       is comparable with that of 16-bit ISA bus peripheral devices.

Table A-1          Compact ISA (CISA) Interface Signals
 Name                   Type*      Description

 MAD[15:0]                1/0      Multiplexed Bus: Used to transfer address, command, data, IRQ, DRQ, DACK information.
 ATCLK                     I       Standard ISA Clock: CISA device uses rising edge to clock in the first (address) phase.
 ALE                       I       Standard ISA Address Latch Enable: CISA peripheral device uses rising edge of ALE to
                                   latch the second (address and command) phase. CISA host uses falling edge of ALE to latch
                                   CMD# from peripheral device.
 CMD#                      I       Command Indication: Common to host and all devices on the CISA bus. The CISA host
                                   asserts CMD# during the data phase of the cycle to time the standard ISA command
                                   (IORD#/WR#, MRD#/WR#), and also asserts CMD# to acknowledge SEL#ATB#.
 SEL#/ATB#                 0       Device Selected I ISA Bus Backoff Request: Common to all peripheral devices on the
 (also CLKRUN#)         Tristate   CISA bus. When ALE is high, the CISA device asserts SEL# to indicate to the host that it is
                                   claiming the cycle. When ALE is low, the CISA device drives this signal to indicate that it has
                                   an interrupt and/or OMA request to make; the host acknowledges by asserting CMD#. After
                                   the host has preset the CISA device in a Stop Clock mode, the device can assert this signal
                                   asynchronously to restart the clock.
 IOCHRDY                   0       Standard ISA Cycle Extension Request: Used during memory and 1/0 cycles.
